subject: general
question: What is the name of a river in central India with a total length of about 724 km, which originates from Betul, Madhya Pradesh, and joins the Arabian Sea?
solution:
The correct answer is "**Tapi River**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tapi River** is a river in central India.
 
• It is one of the major rivers in peninsular India with a length of roughly 724 km and a flow direction from **east to west**.
 
• The Tapi River rises to a height of roughly 752 metres near Multai in the Betul district of **Madhya Pradesh** and flows for a distance of about 724 kilometres before emptying into the **Arabian Sea** through the Gulf of Cambay.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are just three rivers in peninsular India that flow from east to west, the other two being the **Narmada River** and the **Mahi River**.
 
• The second-largest interstate river basin that empties into the west is the Tapi.
 
• It includes a major portion of the state of **Maharashtra** as well as portions of Gujarat and **Madhya Pradesh**.
